question.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{1}{16+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{1}{16\cdot (1+{x}^{2}/16)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}/16}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{1}{1+(x/4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

 

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{4})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{4}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=4\,\text{d}u.
$$

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $2$ |

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{1}{16+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{1}{1+(x/4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (4\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{\text{d}u}{1+{u}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arctan}⁡u{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
